first_impression.reaction: The opening line calls out exactly what I'm suspicious of: "Most advice on choosing a diamond is written by someone with a tray of stones to sell you." Fine, but then what are you selling? "Nothing to sell in the stone itself" reads like a lawyer wrote it. I jumped to the FAQ, it was factual and sourced, so I went back and read the report-checking and Kimberley sections properly.

journey.quote: This diamond buying guide has nothing to sell in the stone itself.
journey.reaction: "In the stone itself" is a careful qualifier. What's the catch? Do you sell something else, or take a referral fee from a jeweller? Say it straight.

journey.section: Diamond grading reports: GIA vs IGI and how to check one
journey.quote: Type the number in yourself, on the lab's own website, rather than following a link or QR code someone hands you.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the kind of practical anti-scam step I actually want. Nobody selling stones tells you to distrust their QR code.

journey.section: Diamond grading reports: GIA vs IGI and how to check one
journey.quote: GIA and IGI are the laboratories you are most likely to see named, and this guide does not rank them.
journey.reaction: Bit of a dodge. Everyone on Reddit argues about this. I don't need a ranking, but tell me if the grades are known to differ between them, or say plainly that you have no data either way.

journey.section: A report is not a valuation
journey.quote: A grading report describes the stone. It does not put a value on it, and it is not an appraisal for insurance
journey.reaction: Useful distinction, and one a jeweller would happily blur.

journey.quote: We found no Australian guidance written specifically for lab-grown diamonds
journey.reaction: Admitting what you couldn't find. That's what makes me believe the rest.

journey.quote: only about 25% to 35% of diamonds show any fluorescence, and more than 95% of those glow blue
journey.reaction: Numbers with a named, linked source. Easy to check, which I will.

journey.quote: So "Kimberley Process compliant" speaks to one specific problem.
journey.reaction: Honest about the limits of the certificate everyone waves around. Strongest section for me.

journey.section: Bow-tie in ovals, pears and marquise
journey.quote: Many jewellers describe a darker, bow-tie shaped area across the middle of some elongated stones
journey.reaction: "Many jewellers describe" is weaker than the rest. Everywhere else you cite GIA; here it's hearsay.

journey.section: Declaring it on return to Australia
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements with you before you travel, as these rules can change.
journey.reaction: A sales line dropped into the customs section. I don't have a Wedded Advisor, and I don't know what one costs. Feels like the upsell starting.

unanswered_questions: How does Wedded Wonderland make money from this, and does it get any commission or referral fee from jewellers it links to or recommends?
What does Wedded Concierge cost, and is it a flat fee or a percentage?
Do you take a cut from venues and vendors you book through Wedded Concierge?
Is there any evidence the GIA and IGI grade differently, or none either way?

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish
turn_offs_found.why: A service promise with no fee, no proof and no example. After a page of sourced facts, the pitch has none.

would_share_with: A mate shopping for a ring, mainly for the report-checking steps and the shortlist checklist

cta_reaction.quote: If the proposal or the wedding is heading overseas, talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: At least it comes after the evidence, not before. But I'd only click to find out the fee model and whether you take supplier commissions, and the page gives me neither.

top_3_changes: Replace "nothing to sell in the stone itself" with a plain statement of how Wedded Wonderland earns money and whether it takes any jeweller referral fees.
Next to the Wedded Concierge CTA, say how the fee works and whether supplier commissions are involved, or link to a page that does.
Cite a named source for the bow-tie point instead of "many jewellers describe", and drop the Wedded Advisor line from the customs section.

checks.check: Every point has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; missing fee and commission details logged as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
